does: Sets beaten eggs into a thin, tender sheet with a creamy middle, and rolls it into a smooth, pale cylinder.

intro.what: This French-style omelette method forms beaten eggs into a pale sheet and rolls it into a smooth cylinder.
intro.why: It teaches you to coordinate stirring, pan movement and folding while controlling surface colour.

how: Heat butter in a pan over medium heat until it foams and the foam starts to fall.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir fast in small circles while shaking the pan.
Stop stirring when the eggs are mostly set but still wet on top, and let the bottom firm for a moment.
Scatter any filling down the middle.
Tilt the pan, fold the near edge over, and roll the omelette to the far lip.
Turn it out onto the plate, seam side down.

cues.text: A pale yellow, smooth skin with no brown. The top still glistens when you start to roll.
The omelette slides freely when the pan is shaken.

mistakes.mistake: The pan is too hot, so the skin browns and turns leathery.
mistakes.fix: Lift the pan off the heat while you stir, and turn the heat down.

mistakes.mistake: Waiting for the top to dry before rolling, which leaves the middle firm and dull.
mistakes.fix: Roll while the top is still wet. The heat inside finishes it.

quiz.question: Which shape and surface does this omelette method aim for?
quiz.because: This French-style omelette is rolled into a smooth cylinder with a pale surface, rather than browned or broken into curds.

quiz.question: After pouring in the eggs, how do you move the eggs and pan?
choices: Leave the pan still and never stir.
Wait for the bottom to brown before moving the eggs.
Stir in small circles while shaking the pan.
quiz.because: Stirring in small circles while shaking the pan helps form the thin sheet that you will roll.

quiz.question: Which pan movement suggests the omelette is free enough to roll?
choices: It slides freely when the pan is shaken.
It stays firmly stuck despite shaking.
Its skin becomes brown and leathery.
quiz.because: An omelette that slides freely is not stuck to the pan, so you can begin folding and rolling it.

quiz.question: The skin is browning and becoming leathery. What should you change?
choices: Raise the heat to speed up the rolling.
Lift the pan off the heat while stirring and turn the heat down.
Press the eggs into the hot pan without moving them.
quiz.because: Excess heat browns and toughens the skin. Lift the pan away while stirring and lower the heat.

comes_after.why: The first half of an omelette is a fast scramble. A cook who can stop a scramble in time can stop an omelette in time.
